approach: Put the retry inside land_pr's check wait in gh.rs. Two methods go on PrHost: `rerun_failed(commit)` POSTs `actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` for the commit's failed workflow runs and returns how many it asked for; `failing_test(commit)` reads the failed check run's job log and parses the first `test x::y ... FAILED` line. After the first bounded wait (the existing Poll, 30 x 20 s), a Red result triggers one rerun and a second bounded wait of the same size, so the total is at most twice the poll. In that second wait a Red seen before any Pending is treated as the old result and ignored. A second Red triggers no rerun; it looks up the failing test name. PrReport gains `rerun: bool` and `failing_test: Option<String>`, which serialize into the JSON report. display::land_pr prints both. The merge gate (merge_via_rest and Green) is untouched. GhClient's `api` is split so a text reply (the log) goes through the same retry, error-log and redaction path as JSON replies.

decisions.choice: The retry lives in land_pr (a new step after wait_for_checks), with the host asked through two new PrHost methods.
decisions.reason: The root cause is that land_pr treats the first Red as final. Fixing it there covers every caller, and a fake PrHost can test it.

rejected.option: Wrapper in Athena::land_pr or main.rs that calls land_pr twice
rejected.why: Re-running the whole flow is not a single rerun of failed jobs, and the fake-PrHost tests could not see it.

rejected.option: Change `checks()` to return a richer struct
rejected.why: Many tests and classify_checks callers depend on Checks. Adding methods is smaller.

decisions.choice: Bound = the existing Poll for each of the two waits, so the total is at most 2 x attempts looks (about 20 min). This is stated in the code and docs.
decisions.reason: It keeps the existing bound and needs no new setting. A test asserts check_reads <= 2*attempts.

rejected.why: A slow first run would leave the rerun almost no time.

decisions.choice: After a rerun, a Red look before any Pending look counts as the stale pre-rerun result and polling continues. The bound still applies.
decisions.reason: GitHub may keep reporting the old failure briefly. Without this, the rerun would be judged Red at once.

rejected.option: Sleep once and trust the next look
rejected.why: Racy, and it gives a false second failure.

decisions.choice: Read the failing test from the job log (`actions/jobs/{check_run_id}/logs`) with a pure parser `failing_test_name(log)`. If no name is found the report carries None and display says no test name was found. Reading it never fails the landing.
decisions.reason: cargo test writes FAILED lines to the log, not to annotations. Check-run ids from the check-runs reply are the Actions job ids.

rejected.why: cargo test emits none by default.

decisions.choice: Use HostOperation::ReadChecks for the rerun POST and the log read.
decisions.reason: The operation list is closed (HostOperation::ALL has 5, and the Pages rerun does the same). Adding a variant would touch athena-data and a stored record format.

rejected.why: Widens the change into athena-data and its parser and tests.

decisions.choice: Split GhClient::api into `api_text` (retry, log, redaction) and `api` (JSON parse of it).
decisions.reason: The log reply is not JSON, and the new calls must use the existing retry path.

rejected.why: Bypasses retry and the error log.

files.purpose: Add PrHost::rerun_failed and failing_test, GhClient impls, api_text, the pure parsers, PrReport fields rerun and failing_test, the retry logic in land_pr, and the FakeHost tests.
Print the rerun and the failing test name for a Red open pull request, plus display tests.
Update the land_pr_code doc: the exit code is unchanged and stays 2 after a second failure. Plus a small test if the JSON print is covered there.
Document that checks_poll is the bound of each of the two waits, so the total is at most twice.
Describe the bounded wait, the single rerun-failed-jobs, the stale-Red rule, and the failing-test report.
Cover the new operations in the retry and error-log tests, and extend the Injecting runner with the runs, rerun-failed-jobs and logs paths.

steps: In gh.rs, split GhClient::api into api_text (the retry loop returning the String) and api (the JSON parse of it).
Add pure parsers: failed_workflow_run_ids(runs reply), failed_check_run_ids(check-runs reply) and failing_test_name(log).

Add PrHost::rerun_failed and PrHost::failing_test. Implement them on GhClient: GET actions/runs?head_sha=…, POST actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs for each failed run, and GET check-runs, then actions/jobs/{id}/logs through api_text, using HostOperation::ReadChecks.
Add rerun: bool and failing_test: Option<String> to PrReport. Update both constructors (confirm_existing_merge gives false and None).
Rework wait_for_checks to take an after_rerun flag with the stale-Red rule. In land_pr, add the single rerun, the second wait and the failing-test lookup, ahead of the unchanged merge gate.
Extend FakeHost with scripted checks, rerun and failing-test fields and counters. Write the tests for criteria 1, 2, 3 and 5 (the parser and client path).
Update display::land_pr and add display tests. Update the doc comments in main.rs and wiring.rs.
Extend external_calls.rs: the Injecting runner paths, the operations() entries, and a land_pr JSON-field check.
Run cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets and cargo test, and fix any warnings.

risks.risk: The rerun doubles the worst-case wait to about 20 minutes.
risks.mitigation: State it in the code and docs. The bound is a test assertion (check_reads <= 2 x attempts).

risks.risk: Existing FakeHost tests and callers break because PrHost gains methods, and PrReport gains fields.
risks.mitigation: The new methods have no default impl, so every implementer is a compile error. Only FakeHost (gh.rs tests) and GhClient implement PrHost, and the PrReport constructors are land_pr and confirm_existing_merge. Keep FakeHost::new(checks) and add a scripted constructor.

risks.risk: Logs may carry secrets or be large.
risks.mitigation: Only the test name is extracted and kept. The log text is never stored or printed. Errors pass through the existing redaction path.

risks.risk: A failure reading the log or rerunning masks the landing result.
risks.mitigation: A failed failing_test lookup becomes None. A rerun error propagates as a host error, like any other host call, and is logged.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in gh.rs with a FakeHost scripted [Red, Pending, Green] and merge_via_rest on. It asserts rerun count == 1, check reads after the rerun, checks == Some(Green), merges == 1, merge_requested and link Landed, and report.rerun == true.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: exactly one rerun_failed call, then a second wait, then the merge.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rerun step the first Red ends the run: rerun count is 0, no merge happens, and checks stay Red.

demonstrations.method: Unit test with a FakeHost scripted Red every time and failing_test returning Some("mod::it_fails"). It asserts rerun_failed was called once, the report has checks Red, rerun true and failing_test == Some("mod::it_fails"), merges == 0, and failing_test was not requested before the second Red. A second case has the fake return None and expects failing_test == None.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: one rerun only, the name is carried on the PrReport, and nothing is merged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the cap a second rerun occurs, or the name is missing from PrReport.

demonstrations.method: Test with a FakeHost that is always Pending, with attempts = 3. It asserts Pending, zero reruns, zero merges, and reads == 3. A second test with Red then Pending forever after the rerun asserts reruns == 1, no merge, and check_reads <= 2*3 using a counting sleep.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: Pending returns without a rerun or merge, and the total number of looks stays within twice the poll.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unbounded or restarted wait would exceed the read count, or a Pending result would trigger a rerun.

demonstrations.method: Display unit tests in display.rs build PrReports: a second failure with rerun true and a test name, and one with no name found. They assert the text contains the test name and 're-run once', and that serde_json::to_value(report) has `failing_test` and `rerun`. A test in external_calls.rs checks the JSON field on a real land_pr result.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: the text names the failing test and states the single rerun, and the JSON has the same fields.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the display and field changes the text keeps 'a check failed; nothing was merged' with no name, and the JSON lacks the keys.

demonstrations.method: Parser tests in gh.rs on sample payloads. `failed_runs` and `failed_check_run_ids` run on a real-shaped actions/runs reply and check-runs reply; `failing_test_name` runs on a sample cargo log that has timestamp prefixes and a `test a::b ... FAILED` line, and on a log with no failure. A FakeRunner test asserts the client POSTs `repos/example/project/actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs`. In external_calls.rs, add the new operations to `operations()` so the one-off-500 retry and persistent-500 error-log tests cover them, and extend the Injecting runner with the new paths.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass: the endpoint path is right, the name is parsed from the sample, and a 500 on the rerun is retried and recorded under ReadChecks.
demonstrations.fails_without: A wrong endpoint or parser makes the path or name assertion fail. A call that bypassed api_text would not be retried, and the retry test would fail.

demonstrations.observes: All tests pass. Then `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` run with no warnings or diffs.

demonstrations.method: Read the docs diff: a new section in docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and an entry at the top of CHANGELOG.md, each naming the wait bound, the single rerun and the failing-test report.
demonstrations.observes: Both files show the text on wait (up to twice 30 x 20 s), one rerun-failed-jobs, the failing test name in the text and JSON, and an unchanged merge gate and exit code.

open_questions: Whether a failure that is a commit status (not an Actions job) can be re-run is unsettled. The plan treats it as nothing to rerun (rerun_failed returns 0): the report has rerun false and the old Red text.

gh api on the job logs endpoint follows the redirect and returns plain text. I did not check this against a real host, so the producer should rely on the sample-log parser test, and a failed log read yields no name.
The Red-before-Pending rule can make a genuine second failure cost a full second wait if the host never shows Pending after the rerun.
